text:
mia: Heads-up — while running a local canary I noticed a small log snippet that looks like a partially redacted customer email plus a session token. Not sure if it's persisted to S3 or just local. Pinging sec and oncall.

sophie: thanks, can you paste the exact line?

mia: here — removing surrounding noise:
```
2026-03-17T14:12:02Z INFO request id=abc123 user_email=***@example.com session=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6...
```

mia: the email was masked but the session token looks like a JWT. unsure if truncated.

diego: tagging @chris_oncall and @leah_legal — important for scoping.

chris_oncall: on it. canary cluster is in us-west-2. mia — do you have the pod/container id? also did you grep S3 buckets?

mia: pod id: canary-77b9; haven't searched S3 yet. I can run a quick grep across the canary logging prefix.

sec-bot: Incident checklist: collector of evidence -> snapshot logs, isolate, rotate keys if secret exposure suspected.

sophie: quick triage Q: token alone may not be usable, but policy requires assuming exposure until proven otherwise. I'd prefer we treat as PII+credentials.

chris_oncall: ok. mia — 1) snapshot the canary logs 2) run `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-canary-logs/2026-03-17/` and `aws s3 cp s3://... ./tmp` for any matches 3) dump pod logs `kubectl logs canary-77b9 > /tmp/canary.log`. Post results here.

mia: doing steps now, will be ~10m.

(7 minutes later)

mia: grep found two objects with that request id in s3: s3://redwood-canary-logs/2026-03-17/abc123.log and archived/abc123.log.gz

mia: copied both locally and searched — token present in both. appears full JWT. Email is masked.

sophie: thanks. treat as session credential exposure. Next steps: 1) rotate any affected session keys (if tied to internal service) 2) redact logs in S3 (overwrite or delete depending on retention) 3) check if token was used in any downstream requests (auth logs) 4) escalate to privacy for comms.

diego: @leah_legal can you advise on customer comms? we need to know if this meets threshold for notification.

leah_legal: thanks for the ping. need scope details: is this a single canary user (internal/test), or does it map to a real customer? if internal only, likely no external notification. if real customer, we need: affected user id, session creation time, and whether token was redeemed.

mia: looks internal — test account email was test+canary@example.com. session was created ~14:10Z. no downstream auth logs show use after that timestamp (quick check).

leah_legal: ok helpful. if it's a test account and no misuse, we can avoid customer notification but still document in incident register and apply remediation and audit. please preserve evidence for 30 days.

chris_oncall: remediation plan: 1) delete/overwrite the two S3 objects (mia to do) 2) deploy a small fix to remove JWT from logs (PR incoming) 3) run a broad grep across last 7 days for similar patterns (diego/mia) 4) add a logging lint rule to prevent token fields from being logged (sophie to own). who can do S3 deletion + evidence backup?

mia: I'll move objects to s3://redwood-incident-evidence/1938765432/ then delete originals. doing that now.

mia: moved and deleted originals. evidence copied to incident bucket with restricted ACLs.

sophie: thanks. please open a PR with the logger change and link it here. keep it small — prefer regex-based mask at source.

diego: I'll run a grep job across prod and canary for `session=[A-Za-z0-9-_\.] {20,}` and report findings in the next hour.

sam_marketing: looping in comms question — if legal gives greenlight, we may want a short internal blurb for CS and a template for customers in case it becomes necessary.

leah_legal: internal-only = no customer notice. please craft an internal blurb after remediation is complete. sam_marketing, i'll review templates if escalation needed.

chris_oncall: decision: treat as limited internal exposure. actions assigned: mia (evidence copy + S3 delete) DONE, diego (search) in progress, sophie (logger PR + lint) assigned, leah_legal (comms hold/review) assigned. reopen if diego finds prod hits.

(30 minutes later)

diego: grep finished — no hits in prod in last 7 days. only canary instances.

sophie: opened PR 2345 with masking at logger. small test added. please review @chris_oncall @mia.

chris_oncall: reviewed, merging now.

mia: thanks everyone. closing thread for now — will document in incident register and tag with privacy-review. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: Incident note: issue recorded as INT-2026-042. evidence bucket: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/1938765432/ — retention 30d, restricted access.
